branch_isolation_evidence: All 13 emitter rows use the literal prefix 'private-branch.' concatenated with a non-null branch_id (Order::branch_id, $event->branchId int-typed, or fan-out across Branch::status=ACTIVE/1).
$event->branchId on ItemExtra/ItemVariation events is typed `int` (non-nullable) — no empty-suffix `private-branch.` channel injection vector.

ItemAvailabilityChanged supports null branchId for global menu changes; in that branch the channel set is constructed from Branch::query()->whereIn('status', [ACTIVE, 1]) — bounded and explicit (PersistItemAvailabilityChangedToOutbox:38-48).

Channel auth callback at routes/channels.php:41-62 enforces user.branch_id == channel.branchId for staff; kiosk tokens are restricted via KioskMachine row lookup (`withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class)`).

channel_auth_bypasses_review.return_true_at_line_57: routes/channels.php:57 contains `return true;` BUT it is INSIDE the conditional `if ($user->hasRole('Admin') || $user->hasRole('Tenant Admin'))` block (line 56). NOT an unconditional bypass. This is the documented Admin/Tenant-Admin cross-branch supervision flow. F-SEC-W6-02 explicitly closed the prior Guest-Echo-Bypass that used a bare `branch_id===0` sentinel.
channel_auth_bypasses_review.kiosk_token_branch_isolation: Token-name discriminator (currentAccessToken()->name === 'kiosk-token') is immune to Sanctum `*` wildcard match. Confirmed by F-SEC-W6-01 heal (2026-05-18).

payload_bloat_candidates.note: Payload includes `$order->token` — this is the per-Order anonymous session token (string, set in OrderService::tokenCreate line 2286/2293, persisted on orders.token + frontend_orders.token columns). It is NOT a Sanctum auth token, but it IS used by guest payment-redirect flows (Stripe/Credit gateways) to authorize follow-up requests on the order. Risk is bounded by branch-channel isolation (only same-branch admin/staff/kiosk receive it) and the field is also exposed via /api/admin/order/{id} so leakage attack surface is consistent with existing REST. Recommend documenting + revisiting under Phase D Sanctum hardening (V1.0.X cloud-prep). NOT a P0/P1 ship blocker.

adversarial_findings.vector: Cross-branch broadcast attempt (admin sends to a wrong branch channel)
adversarial_findings.evidence: All 13 emitter listeners construct channels from server-trusted state (Order::$branch_id PK FK, $event->branchId int-typed, or scoped Branch::query()). No path accepts user-controlled branchId in body. Channel auth at routes/channels.php:41-62 also re-verifies on subscribe-side (defense-in-depth).

EventContract::assertEnvelopeValid (DispatchDomainEventsJob.php:110) enforces V1 envelope shape. Frontend dedupes by `correlation_id` (eventContract.js:103,326-386 — 2048 cap, 10-min TTL, sessionStorage-persisted). Backend writes correlation_id from sharedContext/X-Correlation-ID/Str::uuid (PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox:108-124 pattern). Replayer would need same correlation_id (already deduped) or a forged one (still bound to original branch channel; receivers ignore stale aggregate_id state).

adversarial_findings.vector: Channel name injection (user-controlled string in channel ref)
adversarial_findings.evidence: Channel construction is server-side concatenation `'private-branch.' . (int)$branchId`. No string interpolation from request body. Channel auth wildcard `branch.{branchId}` only accepts integer-shape via type coercion `(int) $branchId` (channels.php:49,61).

adversarial_findings.vector: Echo memory growth over long sessions (4h+ connection)
adversarial_findings.evidence: WebSocketService heartbeat 30s + pongTimeout 5s + activityTimeout 30s + reconnect circuit-breaker (NEW-02). Frontend correlation dedupe has 2048-entry hard cap with FIFO eviction (eventContract.js:99-104). sessionStorage TTL 10min (lines 100-101). KDS adaptive polling tears down on tab close (_pollingInterval cleanup line 2372).
PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedToOutbox:58 includes `$order->token` (Order session token) in payload. Bounded by branch-scoped channel isolation. Listed in payload_bloat_candidates.

adversarial_findings.vector: PHP↔JS BROADCAST_MAP drift (envelope type mismatch warnings)
adversarial_findings.evidence: PHP `EventContract::BROADCAST_MAP` (app/Domain/Events/EventContract.php:34-49) declares 11 entries; JS `BROADCAST_MAP` (resources/js/services/eventContract.js:16-25) declares 7. Missing JS: OrderItemAdded, OrderCancelled, StockLow, OrderPaymentStatusChanged. If any of these are ever subscribed in the frontend, eventContract.js:351-357 logs `console.warn('[eventContract] Event type mismatch for broadcast.')` for every envelope. Contract drift, not a security risk.

verdict_rationale: Topology is structurally sound — single canonical branch-scoped channel, token-name auth discriminator immune to Sanctum wildcard, fan-out via centralized outbox + envelope contract validation, correlation-id dedupe, polling fallback per-surface, F-12 auth-failure sliding window, NEW-02 storm circuit-breaker. No P0/P1 defects. AMBER (not GREEN) because: (1) three outbox rows are emitted with zero Echo listeners (SettingsUpdated, OrderPaymentStatusChanged, BranchStatusChanged) — wasted Pusher frames + latent UX gaps; (2) ComposerProfileChanged Echo binding is dead (server bridges to CatalogChanged); (3) order.token field in OrderPaymentStatusChanged payload is bounded-risk but worth documenting; (4) PHP/JS BROADCAST_MAP contract drift (11 vs 7 entries) emits console.warn for any future subscriber on the 4 missing entries. All four findings are V1.0.2 dead-code cleanup / observability hygiene candidates — none block V1 LOCAL ship.
